name: cpubound
description: Identical CPU-bound handler (~5 ms busy-spin per invocation) on each platform; the SAQEF protocol. Runs are COUNT-BOUND (exactly total requests); duration is a safety cap only.

regression.description: c=4, 8-core bare metal, REPEAT=5, calibrated IDLE_W=4.3. Must reproduce the known-good medians (fn 11.60 / openfaas 7.67) within tolerance_pp, or the refactor is NOT trusted. OpenFaaS runs first, torn down (stack rm + service rm hello), then Fn.
regression.reference_notes: fn reference RECALIBRATED 2026-08-06: the 2026-08-05 value 10.46 is stale for this box. Same-day A/B on an identical fresh-setup Fn run: old runner (run_saqef.sh all) = 11.60, refactored CLI = 11.96 (flat ~11.6-12.1, all 5 runs; known-good ran 9.8-11.7 with the documented fnserver warm-up ramp). Deviation is entirely fnserver per-request CP cost (0.61 -> 0.75 ms) with fn_cpu_s identical (~56.7 s) - a bounded box-state drift, NOT a refactor change (harness argv is byte-identical; see tests/test_saqef_cli.py). openfaas reference unchanged (7.67; measured 7.55 today). PROVENANCE NOTE: these 11.60/7.67 references were established BEFORE the harness diverged from saqef-v2.0-frozen for the carbon unit fix (J/3600->J/3.6e6) and the data-driven isolation guard (--forbidden-services/--forbidden-containers). Those edits touch only the carbon formula and a precondition gate; they cannot move cp_dynamic_share_pct (unit-free cgroup CPU-time ratio; isolation is a check, not sampling math) - but per the trust-gate discipline this file's references are not byte-identical provenance to the current harness, so a REGRESSION RERUN is the gate for trusting the new harness, not this file alone.
